name: Hareli Eco Resort
location: Mohda, inside Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary (~9 km from main entry gate)
why_special: Chhattisgarh Tourism's flagship eco-resort for Barnawapara — 12 double-room cottages set inside the 245 sq km sanctuary, rooms overlook a lake where chital, sambar, nilgai and monkeys visit at dusk. TripAdvisor 4.7/5 across 20 reviews; #1 of 1 ranch in Mahasamund. Bonfire, solar power and open-jeep safaris arranged through the front desk; no cellular network or WiFi inside the property — by design.

name: Barnawapara Forest Rest House
location: Inside Barnawapara Wildlife Sanctuary buffer (CG Forest Department)
why_special: The Forest Department's own rest house and eco-cottages inside the sanctuary — the budget alternative to Hareli and the only stay deeper into the buffer than Mohda. Bookings exclusively via cgforest.com/barnawapara online portal; food-inclusive tariff is the default. Used by foresters, ASI-attached researchers and serious wildlifers who want the 05:30 jeep before tourists arrive.

name: Hiuen Tsiang Tourist Resort
location: Behind Paryatak Suchna Kendra, Near Sirpur Chowk (~800 m / 18-min walk to Lakshmana Temple)
why_special: CGTDC's purpose-built heritage-themed tourist resort at Sirpur — 12 AC/non-AC rooms (some convertible 14x20 with changing area) plus two 15-bed dorms, named for the 7th-century Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who recorded Sirpur in his Da Tang Xiyu Ji. Room 7 is the 'HH Dalai Lama Room' from his Sirpur visit. 300-seater on-site restaurant, party hall and a jogging-track green park; the only sit-down lodging at the site and the only way to be on the monuments at sunrise without driving in from Raipur. TripAdvisor listing currently displays as 'Soumya Resorts' — same property, possible rebranding under operator handover; CGTDC and Yatra still list as Hiuen Tsiang.

name: Aloha Nature Stay
location: Jalki village, on the bank of Sirpur River at the fringe of Barnawapara forest
why_special: 20-room private cottage cluster (nine of them garden-view), on the Sirpur River at the edge of the Barnawapara forest — a 50.3 km / 70-minute drive from Raipur Airport and ~18 minutes to Lakshmana Temple. Standard, Suite and Wooden Suite categories; on-site restaurant cooks tribal-flavoured veg menu from farm-grown organic plot. The pairing for travellers wanting a single-base for both Sirpur archaeology and a Barnawapara morning safari without driving back to Raipur. TripAdvisor 3.7/5 across 6 reviews — small sample but consistent.

name: Dandami Luxury Resort, Chitrakote
location: Dandami Luxury Resort, Tiratha, Chitrakote, Tehsil Lohandiguda, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494223
why_special: CGTDC's flagship resort at Tiratha on the rim of Chitrakote Falls — 38 km from Jagdalpur on the Lohandiguda road. Luxury river-view rooms plus permanent tents, in-house restaurant, open-air amphitheatre and an interpretation centre. The only stay with falls-view rooms at India's widest waterfall (300m horseshoe at peak monsoon flow); CGTDC books direct on +91 91116 69800 when the website portal is down.

name: Hotel Avinash International
location: Chitrakote Rd, Housing Board Colony, Motitalab Para, Jagdalpur, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494001
why_special: 55-room mid-tier business hotel on Chitrakote Road / Bajrang Nagar, 1-minute drive from Dalpat Sagar and 5.3 km from Tiratgarh Falls / Bastar Palace. Rooftop infinity pool with Sky Dhaba rooftop restaurant and a pure-veg The Vegan Story on the lobby — the city-base most travellers actually pick when they're not staying at Chitrakote.

name: Naman Bastar Resort
location: Chitrakoot Road, Village Palli, Dharampura, Jagdalpur, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494005
why_special: Family-run 21-year-old resort on Chitrakote Road at Palli village/Dharampura — the closest real-resort stay to Bastar Palace, with swimming pool, in-house restaurant and the most-recommended Jagdalpur pick on Justdial/Agoda. Owners run a tribal-circuit tour desk for Tirathgarh, Kutumsar Caves and Bastar Dussehra; the choice when you want central Jagdalpur access plus a pool.

name: Bastar Tribal Homestay (Chhote Bodal)
location: Bastar Tribal Homestay, Village Chhote Bodal, Kawalikala, Post Nangur, Jagdalpur, Bastar District, Chhattisgarh 494005
why_special: Eco-architecture homestay run by Shakeel Rizvi (since 2010) at Chhote Bodal village, 23 km from Jagdalpur — mud walls, clay floors, stone roofs, bamboo elements. ₹700/person/night plus meals cooked on wood fire by a women's self-help group, served on Sal-leaf plates. The lived experience of Dhurwa, Bhatra, Muria and Gond tribal life — handicraft workshops, traditional cooking, farm activities, guided forest walks. Tokapal Tribal Market (25km) and Kanger Valley NP (30km) on the same loop.
